Question: Have you ever met a celebrity and found they were much kinder or ruder than you expected?
Answer: I've met a number of legitimately renowned poets and academics in my professional life. Some of them were absolute sweethearts. Many of them weren't. And I could write an answer about inspirational or unfortunate encounters I've had with several of these (and at least one Nobel laureate who was particularly nasty to me), but excepting Alex Johnston, practically no one here would care. Us common folk are inordinately impressed whenever someone rich and/or famous acts like your average decent person. It's revelatory every time it happens, and that's more than a bit sad. Conversely, we revel in the confirmation bias of infamous assholery. So I'm going to give my answer some clickbait graphics, and otherwise, refuse to play along. Additionally, I'm self aware enough to admit that were I ever gifted/cursed with celebrity, I'd probably tend towards the Chevy Chase end of the spectrum as opposed to the Keanu Reeves side. (sorry about that) This answer will get a lot of views because it has pictures of Keanu Reeves in it.

Question: If Jesus died for our sins, why do we still go to hell for our Sins?
Answer: The whole “savior” business is a pretty raw deal for all involved. Christians are expected to show fealty to a demigod/avatar for which there's no definitive historical evidence one ever even existed. Said son is ostensibly the victim of (at the very least) paternal neglect and (arguably) outright murder by a dad more concerned with filial obedience and the subjugation of underlings than mutual respect and devotion. (And if one adheres to the source material, the whole business is preordained anyway…how this is intended to be indicative of sacrifice and salvation is unapparent to anyone paying the least bit of attention.) I'd more readily worship trees or changes in the weather than a variegated godhead. The former provides life sustaining oxygen and the latter kills exclusively sans ulterior motive. The Trinity only serves to muck things up.

Question: How do I do 3-6 in county jail for the first time?
Answer: For the first time? I'm sorry, Bill Zuccaro, but are you planning on making a career out of this, Sunshine? I'm gonna assume that since you're still posting, you've been convicted and given a report date. And since 3 - 6 is pretty much of a cakewalk sentence, whatever you did probably wasn't all that heinous, and you could potentially qualify for work release. So if your legal counsel hasn't already coordinated that with the judge and the sheriff's department, see if that's a possibility retroactively. And if not, better brush up on your game of Spades, ‘cause you're gonna be spending a lot of time at a day room table trading tricks for commissary snacks. Let the people at work know. I was sort of surprised at how understanding businesses could be in that regard, until I started reporting to work from the jailhouse myself, and realized that a work release employee is about as close to an indentured servant as your boss is likely to employ nowadays. Nobody on work release calls in sick. Nobody on work release lays out drunk of a Monday morning after a lost weekend. You might as well be wearing a shock collar and plow horse tack. You're safe money. Also, if you're on the outs with friends and family over all this, then you better make amends real quick, since nothing is more pitiful in lockup than an inmate without an outside support network. You don't get mail. You don't get visits. You don't get deposits to your commissary account. And there's no one you can call on the pod payphone. My second cellmate was in that very situation after he got pulled from work release for showing up late (and high) for processing on a Friday evening. Jail is what you make it. Don't make it any worse than it absolutely has to be. Collect your shit and keep it together.

Question: Why does Trump keep bringing up Hannibal Lecter?
Answer: Donald Trump idolizes ruthless strongmen to the point of hero worship, and Hannibal Lecter is the archetype: part John Kramer, part Michael Myers, and — for all intents and purposes — a hypersensitive superhuman dynamo, both intellectually and physically. But all Trump himself can manage by way of emulation is the Hannibal blood thirst. Hell…he's not even mentally and emotionally sophisticated enough to understand that Lecter is a character created by novelist Thomas Harris and brought to life on the screen by Sir Anthony Hopkins as opposed to an actual real life serial killer psychologist. Trump keeps referring to “the late great Hannibal Lecter” which is doubly confounding since the doctor in both the books and on screen never dies, plus Tony Hopkins, who portrayed him so convincingly in the movies, is still very much alive himself. (puzzling) I think Trump longs to be imposingly formidable, yet all he can manage is corpulent repellence. He's Buffalo Bill in a fat suit…all ghoulish and disgusting. (“It puts the lotion on its skin….”)
